purpose: Candidate list of additional LIMITED-support Indian crops for the cropRegistry seed, per docs/product/crop-support-matrix.md ('Other known crops (registry seed ~20 more) | LIMITED'). Nothing here is approved and nothing here should be seeded until a human signs off.

rules.noInventedNumbers: No Kc, root depth, depletion fraction, yield, NPK or duration value appears in this file. LIMITED crops take crop-family Kc defaults, so only a sourced `family` is proposed.
rules.citationShape: { org, title, url, accessed, confidence, note }. `sourceRef` is always an ARRAY of that shape.
rules.hindi: EVERY Hindi term is marked hiVerified: false. None of these 21 crops appears in docs/i18n/agricultural-terminology.md (that table covers only the 9 core crops), so no term here can be marked verified. CLAUDE.md rule 8 requires human sign-off on agronomic Hindi before demo.
rules.seasonEnum: KHARIF | RABI | ZAID. The Government of India sources print 'Kharif', 'Rabi', 'Summer', 'Spring/Summer', 'Pre Rabi' and 'Early kharif'. 'Summer' and 'Spring/Summer' are recorded as ZAID; that mapping is a naming decision, NOT a claim made by the source. The source's own wording is preserved in every citation note.

selectionCriteria: The crop is named in the Government of India MSP statement (the 22 MSP-mandated crops — GoI's own definition of the crops that are major by value), OR
the crop has its own sheet/column in the DES 'Crop Calendar of Major Crops' (Appendix IV, sourced to ICAR Crop Science Division), which is GoI's own definition of India's major crops.
The 9 crops already at SPECIALIZED/GENERAL level (rice, wheat, maize, cotton, soybean, tomato, potato, onion, chilli) are excluded.
Copra was excluded: it is a processed product (dried coconut kernel), not a field crop with a sowing season.
unverifiedClaims: MANDI PRESENCE IS NOT VERIFIED. The brief asked to prefer crops that also appear in mandi price data. That could not be confirmed: agmarknet.gov.in is now a JavaScript single-page app that serves no server-rendered commodity list, and the data.gov.in Agmarknet resource needs an API key that this project does not yet have (OD-5 is still open). No `mandiCommodity` field is therefore asserted for any crop here.
MSP inclusion is used as evidence that a crop is major by value in India. It is NOT evidence that the crop appears in the Agmarknet commodity vocabulary.

Season is read from the explicit column-header row of each sheet; the sheet number and header text are named in each citation below.

FAO56_TABLE_12.title: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 — Crop Evapotranspiration, Chapter 6, TABLE 12. Single (time-averaged) crop coefficients, Kc, and mean maximum plant heights
FAO56_TABLE_12.note: Used ONLY for the `family` field. FAO-56 Table 12 organises crops into lettered groups (a. Small Vegetables, e. Legumes (Leguminosae), g. Fibre Crops, h. Oil Crops, i. Cereals, k. Sugar Cane, ...) and prints a representative Kc triple on each group heading row. That group is exactly the right handle for the 'crop-family Kc defaults' that LIMITED crops are specified to use.

familyFieldConvention.family: The FAO-56 Table 12 group heading the crop sits under. Populated only where FAO-56 lists the crop (or its exact English name) itself.
familyFieldConvention.faoTable12Row: The literal Table 12 row name, when FAO-56 lists this crop by name.
familyFieldConvention.proposedFaoProxy: Set instead of faoTable12Row when FAO-56 has NO row for the crop and a related row is being proposed as the family-default donor. Every one of these is a proposal requiring approval — FAO-56 makes no such equivalence.

gaps.field: names.hi for HORSEGRAM, FIELDPEA, CASTOR, LINSEED, SUGARCANE
gaps.problem: These five are not MSP crops, so they do not appear in the bilingual MSP statement — the only Government of India document in this research pass that publishes Devanagari crop names.
gaps.tried: Searched the DES crop calendar workbook (English only) and docs/i18n/agricultural-terminology.md (covers only the 9 core crops).
gaps.resolution: names.hi recorded as null. Common Hindi terms exist for all five, but writing them here would be an unsourced agronomic translation, which CLAUDE.md rule 8 and the no-invention rule both forbid. A Hindi-literate reviewer should supply them.

gaps.problem: The official Hindi MSP PDF embeds a legacy non-Unicode Devanagari font; its text layer extracts corrupted (observed: 'Ïवार' for ज्वार, 'मÈका' for मक्का, 'Ǔतल' for तिल, 'रामǓतल' for रामतिल, 'कुसुʁ' for कुसुम्भ, 'सरसɉ' for सरसों).
gaps.tried: pypdf/PyMuPDF text extraction (corrupted), then rendering page 1 of the official PDF at 6x and reading the glyphs visually.
gaps.resolution: All 16 Devanagari names come from the visual read of the official document. This is a real transcription-risk surface and is an additional reason every term is marked hiVerified: false.

gaps.problem: Neither GoI source uses the word 'Zaid'. They use 'Summer', 'Spring/Summer' and 'Pre Rabi'.
gaps.tried: Read every season column header in all 12 sheets of the crop calendar workbook.
gaps.resolution: 'Summer' and 'Spring/Summer' mapped to ZAID; the source wording is preserved verbatim in each citation note. 'Pre Rabi' (sesame only) has no enum member and is dropped. If the registry needs to be faithful to the source vocabulary, the enum should gain a SUMMER member instead.

gaps.problem: This list is entirely field crops. High-value horticultural crops that are prominent in mandi data (banana, mango, turmeric, garlic, brinjal, okra, cabbage, cauliflower, coriander, cumin) are absent.
gaps.tried: The two Government of India sources used here — the MSP statement and the DES crop calendar — cover field crops only. No equally citable GoI source giving both crop identity and season for horticultural crops was located in this pass.
gaps.resolution: Deliberately omitted rather than added from memory. A follow-up pass against a horticulture source (e.g. NHB / 'Horticultural Statistics at a Glance') would be needed.

gaps.problem: Codes are proposed, not sourced. The brief asked for UPPERCASE English codes, but several crops are known in India by their Hindi name (Jowar, Bajra, Ragi, Arhar, Moong, Urad, Masur) and the MSP statement itself uses those Hindi-origin names as its English labels.
gaps.tried: n/a — a naming decision, not a data lookup.
gaps.resolution: English botanical names used for the code (SORGHUM, PEARLMILLET, FINGERMILLET, PIGEONPEA, GREENGRAM, BLACKGRAM, LENTIL) with the GoI label kept in names.en and the alternatives in altNamesEn. A reviewer may prefer codes that match the MSP/Agmarknet labels instead — that choice interacts with the market alias map.

gaps.problem: desagri.gov.in presents an incomplete certificate chain; WebFetch failed with 'unable to get local issuer certificate'.
gaps.tried: WebFetch first, then curl with certificate verification relaxed.
gaps.resolution: All desagri.gov.in documents in this file were fetched over HTTPS with verification relaxed. Contents were sanity-checked (correct GoI page structure, expected table shape, ICAR attribution footers), but this is worth knowing if these fetches are ever automated.
